data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者从Emacs转向Obsidian的经历和原因。Emacs是一个强大但复杂的文本编辑器，具备如Org-Mode等工具，可以用于代码管理、任务跟踪和笔记管理等，但需要大量自定义和插件维护。作者最终因不想再花费精力处理这些复杂配置，转而使用更现代、简便的工具Obsidian。Obsidian是一款基于Markdown的笔记应用，拥有丰富的社区插件支持，且移动端体验更佳。作者计划采用PARA方法（项目、领域、资源、归档）在Obsidian中管理个人知识，以实现更简单和一致的工作流程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Emacs、Obsidian等工具在知识管理、笔记整理以及AI辅助方面的使用体验和争议

不同观点：
• 关于Emacs的使用体验：
  - [8s2ngy]认为Emacs功能强大但需要大量插件和自定义配置，最终让他感到疲倦，尤其是在生活节奏加快、时间有限的情况下。
  - [8s2ngy]的另一面观点：另一位用户表示Emacs不需要大量插件，少量配置即可满足需求，如Magit、Org-mode等工具可以有效提高效率。他认为只需一次性调整配置，之后使用起来很顺畅。

• 关于Obsidian的讨论：
  - [agnishom]质疑Obsidian是否能替代Org-Mode，认为Obsidian不是开源软件，且由少数人维护，存在公司倒闭的风险。不过，他对Obsidian比其他风投支持的工具更有信心。
  - [exiguus]关注Obsidian的加密和自托管问题，几年前因缺乏这些功能而放弃使用，询问现在是否有解决方案。

• 关于AI在笔记和知识管理中的作用：
  - [jiri]担心在AI时代是否应该将个人聊天记录存储在个人知识系统中，并讨论了是否应该重复询问AI同一问题还是查找历史记录。
  - [ebiester]认为AI在组织笔记方面还不够成熟，主要问题在于笔记是为个人而非他人写的，搜索时缺乏上下文。
  - [kreyenborgi]使用Emacs中的gptel工具，将聊天记录和网页摘录一起作为笔记存储，认为这是AI时代的知识管理方式。
  - [bachmeier]强调AI工具只能作为辅助，核心价值在于个人思考，不应该完全依赖AI。
  - [cratermoon]通过实验发现将笔记输入LLM模型并未提供新的见解，反而需要重新解读AI生成的内容，认为手动整理笔记更有助于学习和理解。

补充讨论：
• [sorokod]推荐了文章《You'll Never Think Alone》作为相关阅读材料。
• [crashabr]提到自己正在Logseq上设置PARA系统，呼应了关于不同工具使用的讨论。
• [awinter-py]以幽默方式吐槽Emacs用户使用类似《白鲸》的开头句式，虽然与主要讨论点无关，但反映了社区内一些文化现象。

争议焦点：
• Emacs是否需要大量插件和自定义配置才能高效使用。
• Obsidian作为非开源工具是否值得信任，尤其是在长期数据保存和隐私保护方面。
• AI在知识管理和笔记整理中的实际效果和价值，是否应该完全依赖AI工具还是以个人思考为主。

44214481.article_content:
The Joy (and pain) of Emacs
​
I use emacs, which might be thought of as a thermonuclear word processor.
—Neal Stephenson,
In the Beginning was the Command Line
Some years ago, I went through a phase that I imagine many software developers go through at least once in their careers—a period of intense fascination with
Emacs
. "Emacs is a great operating system that only lacks a decent text editor", as the old joke goes. This rang fairly true in my own experience. Emacs is ostensibly a text editor, but really it is a gateway to a whole world of text-based, flexible tools for managing data of various kinds. Tools like
Magit
and
Org-mode
offered (and still offer) unique ways to make sense of a codebase, track tasks, manage notes, automate and integrate with other systems, etc. This was "personal computing" at its purest; most modern GUI productivity apps felt like toys in comparison.
Emacs is a powerful tool, but it also demands a lot from its user. Eventually I got tired of dealing with the host of plugins and customizations that I needed to keep my system running the way I wanted. I'm at a point in my life where I would rather spend my spare time on hobbies, hanging out with family and friends, and otherwise not messing around with a patchwork of ELisp code snippets that I've cobbled together from various sources. I gradually stopped using Emacs in favor of more modern tools that are less flexible but also less of a hassle.
However, I often found myself missing some of the features that Emacs provided –
Org-Mode
in particular. Org-Mode is a tool for writing hierarchical text documents, and can serve as the foundation for an entirely text-based workflow for note-taking, agendas, and various forms of personal knowledge management. Once you get the hang of it, it's very intuitive. Some people manage their entire lives through Org-Mode and use it to have years of information at their fingertips.
Obsidian: An Org-Mode replacement?
​
I'm currently in the process of preparing for a new role on a new team at my job, and I have a lot of projects to get up to speed on. Enter
Obsidian
: a markdown-based text editor and note-taking app that has a lot of features useful for "personal knowledge management". Obsidian is proprietary software, but like Emacs it has an extensive system of
community-provided plugins
that support all kinds of different workflows (currently I'm using the
Tasks
and
Dataview
plugins, both of which let you dynamically aggregate different kinds of content from across documents in one place). Unlike Emacs, out-of-the-box usage of Obsidian is very straightforward (there's even a good Vim mode!), and there is a well-designed iOS client as well (the lack of an easy way to see tasks on a mobile device was one of the biggest limitations of Org-Mode in my experience).
Like Emacs, Obsidian can be used in a lot of different ways. If I'm going to be successful with this tool, I need to have a vision for how I want to use it. I did a little bit of research about frameworks for personal knowledge management and came across the
PARA
method. The basic idea behind PARA is that you file all your various notes or documents into 4 distinct folders:
Projects
(actionable, short-term),
Areas
(long-term responsibilities or recurring work),
Resources
(useful info to reference later), and
Archive
(anything from any other category that is no longer active). Uncategorized notes typically go into a dedicated inbox folder, and then get organized during a weekly review session. The system seems pretty simple, which I hope will help with being consistent over time. I'd rather have a simple system that I can consistently apply as opposed to a complicated one that I give up on after a few months. PARA is software-independent but it's easy to implement in Obsidian – a "vault" in Obsidian is just a collection of folders and files. My top-level vault structure looks like this:
00 Inbox/
01 Projects/
02 Areas/
03 Resources/
04 Archive/
Attachments/
Templates/
DASHBOARD.md
README.md
TODO.md
In addition to the PARA folders (which are numbered to keep them in the desired order) I have an Inbox, an "attachments" directory (Obsidian will put any attached files there automatically, keeping the rest of the structure uncluttered), a "templates" directory for re-usable content, and a small number of top-level files – a dashboard that pulls together items from various places (using the Dataview plugin), a master todo list (which pulls in tasks from all documents and organizes them, using the Tasks plugin), and a README file to remind me how things are structured. Everything else lives on one of these folders – typically the Inbox first, and then one of the PARA folders after review.
We'll see how well this works in practice, but this is my plan for now.
Why bother doing this?
​
I mentioned above that I stopped using Emacs because I no longer wished to spend the time or effort in fine-tuning and maintaining the custom workflows I was relying on. S

data.article_summary: 日本研究团队开发出一种以植物纤维素为基础的透明纸张，作为塑料的替代品。这种材料可生物降解，生产过程中的碳排放较低。通过将棉籽纤维制成的纤维素粉末溶解在溴化锂溶液中并加热成胶状，再进行成型和干燥，研究人员制造出了厚度为0.7毫米的透明纸张。这种纸张能被微生物分解，即使在757米深的海底，四个月内也能基本降解。该材料有望解决纸包装无法展示内容物的问题，并且其生产成本约为普通纸张的三倍，但碳排放量仅为塑料的一半。专家认为，这种透明纸在深海中的生物降解性是其主要优势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：塑料替代品的可行性及相关问题

不同观点：
• fastball认为，塑料的受欢迎原因在于其轻便和耐用，特别是能持续几千年。他建议开发一种在常规条件下不降解、但在特定触发条件下快速降解的材料。
• kazinator和wolfi1提到历史上存在的纤维素类材料，如赛璐玢（celluloid）和透明纸（cellophane），暗示这些可能已经是可行的替代品。
• pupppet批评一些国家将垃圾倾倒进海洋的问题，并质疑通过创造更好的垃圾来解决环境问题的思路。
• Leo-thorne和Huxley1分享了其实际尝试替代塑料包装的经验，提到可降解材料在成本和性能上的挑战，但对透明纸（ cellulose-based materials）抱有希望。
• NotAnOtter强调成本和耐用性是塑料广泛应用的关键因素，认为目前提出的替代品在经济和功能上无法完全取代塑料。
• yoko888从健康和环境角度出发，认为减少塑料使用不仅有利于环境，也有益于人体健康，支持探索替代材料。
• speedylight呼吁开发具有塑料特性但可快速降解或易回收的新材料。
• hereme888认为即使替代材料不能完全取代塑料，也能在一次性产品领域取得显著进展。
• Beijinger通过引用文章，引发对塑料对人类健康影响的讨论。
• 1970-01-01对某些具体产品如吸管持批评态度，认为并非所有替代品都合适。
• JumpCrisscross对透明纸的制造工艺表示兴趣，特别是如何排列纳米纤维以实现透明性。
• smolder提出应优先将石油用于制造难以替代的材料，如医药，同时通过可再生能源替代石油能源使用。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于替代材料的成本、性能和实际应用效果。
• 讨论中多次提到历史上的纤维素类材料，质疑是否需要全新材料或技术。
• 健康和环境问题被认为是推动塑料替代品研究的重要动力。
• 对新材料的期望包括在常规条件下保持稳定，在特定条件下快速降解。

44205282.article_content:
Technology
Japanese Researchers Develop ‘Transparent Paper’ as Alternative to Plastics; New Material Is Biodegradable, Can Be Produced with Low Carbon Emissions
Post
Share
Post
Photos courtesy of JAMSTEC
Scenery 100 meters away is seen through a sheet of transparent paper which is 0.7 millimeters thick.
The Yomiuri Shimbun
14:47 JST, June 5, 2025
A team of researchers with the Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology (JAMSTEC) and other entities have developed thick sheets of transparent paper using cellulose, a material made from plant biomass.
The transparent paper sheets can be broken down by microbes into water and carbon dioxide. Also, they can be used to make containers because they are thicker than conventional cellulose-based materials. The new material is expected to replace plastics for this purpose, as plastics are a source of ocean pollution.
To make the paper sheets, the team used cellulose powder made from fibers found on the surfaces of cotton seeds. They dissolved the powder in a lithium bromide-water solution, mixing it in as they raised it to a high temperature until it became a gel, at which point the material was shaped and dried.
When the researchers shaped the material into cups and straws, they found that it was about as strong as polycarbonate, a type of plastic.
The paper sheets become transparent because they are packed tightly with nanometer-scale (one 1-billionth of a meter) fibers. The concentration of these fibers allows light to pass straight through the sheets without experiencing diffusion.
Even a sheet of the transparent paper that is 0.7 millimeters thick remains flexible, and scenery 100 meters away can be clearly seen through it.
On the assumption that the paper sheets will be washed into the ocean, the team investigated its biodegradability. The researchers sank the paper sheets into the ocean and checked whether microbes there were able to dissolve them.
The results showed that the deeper the place under the sea was, the slower the dissolution progressed, because there are fewer microbes in the deep ocean. But the paper sheets were mostly dissolved within four months even at 757 meters below the surface.
Photos courtesy of JAMSTEC
A cup and a straw made of the newly developed transparent paper
So far, paper packs have been the most common alternatives to plastic containers.
But business experts have pointed out that consumers are less willing to buy goods in paper packs because they cannot see the contents.
Transparent paper could overcome this problem, but bringing the material to market will require factories with the technology to mass-produce it.
Noriyuki Isobe, a deputy chief researcher for JAMSTEC, said, “If a plant for demonstration experiments of the technology is built, we estimate that the cost to produce the material will be about three times that of ordinary paper, while the volume of CO2 emissions can be kept to about half that of the plastic making process.”
Prof. Masaya Nogi of the University of Osaka, an expert on wooden materials, said, “There have been other types of transparent paper in the past, but the advantage of this over those is that it has been proven to be biodegradable in the deep sea.”

data.title: The Illusion of Thinking: Strengths and Limitations of Reasoning Models
data.author: k1m
data.article_summary: 文章《The Illusion of Thinking: Understanding the Strengths and Limitations of Reasoning Models via the Lens of Problem Complexity》探讨了前沿语言模型中的大型推理模型（LRMs）在处理复杂问题时的表现。尽管LRMs在推理基准测试中表现出色，但其基本能力、扩展特性及局限性尚未完全理解。研究通过可控的 puzzle 环境系统地分析了这些模型在面对不同复杂度问题时的表现，发现LRMs在超出一定复杂度后准确率急剧下降，且存在反直觉的扩展限制：推理 effort 随复杂度增加到某点后反而下降。研究比较了LRMs与其标准LLM对应模型，识别出三种性能模式：低复杂度任务中标准模型表现更好，中等复杂度任务中LRMs有优势，高复杂度任务中两者都表现不佳。研究还揭示了LRMs在精确计算和推理一致性方面的不足，提出了对其真正推理能力的质疑。

The Illusion of Thinking: Understanding the Strengths and Limitations of Reasoning Models via the Lens of Problem Complexity
Authors
Parshin Shojaee*â , Iman Mirzadeh*, Keivan Alizadeh, Maxwell Horton, Samy Bengio, Mehrdad Farajtabar
View publication
Copy Bibtex
Recent generations of frontier language models have introduced Large Reasoning Models
(LRMs) that generate detailed thinking processes before providing answers. While these models
demonstrate improved performance on reasoning benchmarks, their fundamental capabilities, scal-
ing properties, and limitations remain insufficiently understood. Current evaluations primarily fo-
cus on established mathematical and coding benchmarks, emphasizing final answer accuracy. How-
ever, this evaluation paradigm often suffers from data contamination and does not provide insights
into the reasoning tracesâ structure and quality. In this work, we systematically investigate these
gaps with the help of controllable puzzle environments that allow precise manipulation of composi-
tional complexity while maintaining consistent logical structures. This setup enables the analysis
of not only final answers but also the internal reasoning traces, offering insights into how LRMs
âthinkâ. Through extensive experimentation across diverse puzzles, we show that frontier LRMs
face a complete accuracy collapse beyond certain complexities. Moreover, they exhibit a counter-
intuitive scaling limit: their reasoning effort increases with problem complexity up to a point, then
declines despite having an adequate token budget. By comparing LRMs with their standard LLM
counterparts under equivalent inference compute, we identify three performance regimes: (1) low-
complexity tasks where standard models surprisingly outperform LRMs, (2) medium-complexity
tasks where additional thinking in LRMs demonstrates advantage, and (3) high-complexity tasks
where both models experience complete collapse. We found that LRMs have limitations in exact
computation: they fail to use explicit algorithms and reason inconsistently across puzzles. We
also investigate the reasoning traces in more depth, studying the patterns of explored solutions
and analyzing the modelsâ computational behavior, shedding light on their strengths, limitations,
and ultimately raising crucial questions about their true reasoning capabilities.
*Equal contribution.

data.title: Prompting Techniques for Secure Code Generation
data.author: saikatsg
data.article_summary: 这篇文章系统地研究了不同提示技术对大型语言模型（LLM）生成安全代码的影响。通过文献综述，作者识别并评估了几种用于代码生成任务的提示技术，尤其是在GPT-3、GPT-3.5和GPT-4模型上。研究使用了一个包含150个自然语言安全相关代码生成提示的数据集。结果显示，某些技术如“递归批评与改进（RCI）”能有效减少代码中的安全漏洞。文章为LLM生成代码的安全性提供了重要见解，并分类和评估了适用于安全代码生成的提示技术。研究部分由欧盟项目Sec4AI4Sec资助，并已被ACM软件工程与方法论期刊接受。

Title:
Prompting Techniques for Secure Code Generation: A Systematic Investigation
Authors:
Catherine Tony
,
Nicolás E. Díaz Ferreyra
,
Markus Mutas
,
Salem Dhiff
,
Riccardo Scandariato
View a PDF of the paper titled Prompting Techniques for Secure Code Generation: A Systematic Investigation, by Catherine Tony and 3 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Large Language Models (LLMs) are gaining momentum in software development with prompt-driven programming enabling developers to create code from natural language (NL) instructions. However, studies have questioned their ability to produce secure code and, thereby, the quality of prompt-generated software. Alongside, various prompting techniques that carefully tailor prompts have emerged to elicit optimal responses from LLMs. Still, the interplay between such prompting strategies and secure code generation remains under-explored and calls for further investigations. OBJECTIVE: In this study, we investigate the impact of different prompting techniques on the security of code generated from NL instructions by LLMs. METHOD: First we perform a systematic literature review to identify the existing prompting techniques that can be used for code generation tasks. A subset of these techniques are evaluated on GPT-3, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4 models for secure code generation. For this, we used an existing dataset consisting of 150 NL security-relevant code-generation prompts. RESULTS: Our work (i) classifies potential prompting techniques for code generation (ii) adapts and evaluates a subset of the identified techniques for secure code generation tasks and (iii) observes a reduction in security weaknesses across the tested LLMs, especially after using an existing technique called Recursive Criticism and Improvement (RCI), contributing valuable insights to the ongoing discourse on LLM-generated code security.

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了业余无线电爱好者对GPS和GLONASS卫星的接收兴趣及技术挑战。GPS和GLONASS是美国的全球定位系统和俄罗斯的全球导航卫星系统，最初为军用，但如今民用更为广泛。这些系统提供高精度的位置（约50米误差）、时间（100纳秒以内）和频率（10^-12），适用于多种用户，包括无线电爱好者。文章详细描述了卫星广播的信号、GPS/GLONASS接收器的工作原理，以及自制接收器的实际构造和软件操作。接收器可作为独立便携设备或插件模块使用，能提供精确的频率源，并应用于天线指向等场景。

A homemade receiver for GPS & GLONASS satellites
Matjaz Vidmar, S53MV (ex YU3UMV, YT3MV)
1. Introduction to GPS & GLONASS
Radio amateurs have always been interested in space
technology, since the latter strongly depends on reliable
radio communications. Of course radio amateurs are not
only interested in amateur-radio satellites: almost any
artificial Earth's satellite represents a challenge, either to
receive its weak signal on rather high frequencies or to
demodulate, decode and use the data it is transmitting.
Besides amateur-radio satellites, the most interesting
satellites for radio amateurs are weather (imaging) satellites:
radio amateurs have successfully built weather-satellite image
reception equipment for all known weather satellites and all
known image transmission standards. Radio-amateurs also
pioneered satellite TV reception using small antennas much
earlier than this became a mass-produced consumer product.
Although the first navigation satellites were launched
more than 30 years ago, satellite navigation and positioning
has only become popular in the last few years with the
introduction of reliable, accurate and easy-to-use systems
like the american Global Positioning System (GPS) and the
russian GLObal NAvigation Satellite System (GLONASS).
Both are intended to replace a variety of ground-based
radio-navigation aids and as a side product, to provide any
suitably equipped user with very accurate time (100ns) and
very accurate frequency (10^-12).
Although both GPS and GLONASS are primarily intended
for military users, there are already more civilian users of
these systems. GPS (and soon combined GPS/GLONASS) navigation
receivers can be made small, light-weight, easy-to-operate
and inexpensive like VHF FM "handy-talkie" transceivers.
Since these receivers can measure their tri-dimensional
position with an accuracy of around 50m anywhere on the
Earth's surface, their user community ranges from
pleasure-aircraft pilots to truck drivers and mountain
climbers and, why not, radio amateurs!
Besides the challenge to build a satellite receiver
radio amateurs can use GPS and GLONASS signals in other ways
as well. The most immediate application of a GPS or GLONASS
receiver is certainly as a highly accurate frequency source.
Accurate timing and synchronization may be required for
advanced communication techniques like coherent communications
or to seriously investigate the propagation path and the
propagation mechanism of radio waves. Finally, positioning
and direction-finding may be useful for high-gain microwave
antenna pointing.
In this article I am first going to describe the
satellites and the radio signals they are broadcasting.
Further I am going to describe the principles of operation of
a GPS or GLONASS receiver. Finally I am going to describe the
practical construction of homemade GPS and GLONASS receivers,
together with their operating software. These receivers can
be built in two different forms: as stand alone, portable
receivers with a small keyboard and a LCD display, or as
peripherals with their own plug-in modules for the "DSP
computer" described in [1] and [2].
2. GPS & GLONASS system description
2.1. Radio-navigation principles
Radio navigation evolved together with other applications
of radio waves. The operation of all radio-navigation systems
is based on the assumption that the propagation mechanism of
radio waves is well known and that the propagation speed of
radio waves is usually very close to the speed of light in free
space. Further, systems using radio waves usually have a
sufficient range to be practically usable for position,
velocity and attitude determination of a remotely-located
user. Finally, all of the measurements on radio waves, like
direction finding, time-delay measurements, phase measurements
or Doppler-shift measurements, can be performed with simple
and inexpensive technical means at least on the user side.
Early radio-navigation systems used the directional
properties of the receiving antenna, transmitting antenna or
both. In these systems the main sources of measurement errors
are the inaccuracies of the antenna pattern(s). Since the
measured quantity is an angle, the position error grows
linearly with increasing the distance between the remote user
at an unknown location and the navigation equipment at known
location(s). Such systems are therefore severely limited in
either the range or the accuracy and are only efficient to
bring a user to a single point, like bringing an aircraft to
the beginning of a landing runway using the Instrumented
Landing System (ILS).
Time or frequency are certainly the physical quantities
that can be measured most accurately. If the propagation speed
and propagation mode of radio waves are known, one can easily
compute the distance from a time-delay measurement. Further,

data.title: What's a healthy amount of sleep? It differs from one country to another
data.author: XzetaU8
data.article_summary: 新不伦瑞克大学的研究发现，不同国家的人所需的健康睡眠时间存在显著差异，挑战了人人需要相同睡眠时间的观念。研究分析了20个国家近5000人的睡眠数据和健康结果，发现各国平均睡眠时间不同，例如日本为6小时18分钟，法国为7小时52分钟，加拿大为7小时27分钟。研究还表明，遵循文化 norms 的睡眠时间与更好的健康状况相关，建议公共健康指南应根据不同文化的睡眠习惯进行调整。这项研究强调了文化背景在睡眠建议中的重要性。

What’s a healthy amount of sleep? It differs from one country to another
New research challenges the common belief that everyone needs the same amount of sleep for good health.
Erik Rolfsen
May 8, 2025
Your optimal amount of sleep may depend on where you live, new University of British Columbia research has found.
An analysis of sleep data and health outcomes for nearly 5,000 people in 20 countries revealed that the hours of sleep required for good health varies significantly across different cultures, challenging the common belief that everyone needs the same amount.
“Despite the common advice to get eight hours of sleep, our findings suggest that sleep recommendations need to be adjusted based on cultural norms,” said Dr. Steven Heine, professor of social and cultural psychology at UBC and senior author of the
study
published Tuesday in
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
(
PNAS)
. “There is no one-size-fits-all amount of sleep that works for everyone.”
Average sleep duration by country, with France reporting the most sleep and Japan the least. Credit: Erik Rolfsen/UBC Media Relations.
The study confirmed previous findings that average sleep time can vary widely from country to country. For example, the average in Japan was six hours and 18 minutes, while in France it was seven hours and 52 minutes. In Canada, it was seven hours and 27 minutes.
Other studies have found links between shorter sleep durations and poor health outcomes. However, this collaboration between UBC and University of Victoria researchers was the first to investigate whether people from countries with shorter sleep durations suffer from worse health.
The researchers found no evidence that people in countries with less sleep were less healthy than those in longer-sleeping nations.
“People who slept closer to their own culture’s norms for sleep duration tended to have better overall health,” said Dr. Christine Ou, assistant professor in the school of nursing at UVic and the study’s lead author. “This suggests that the ideal amount of sleep is the amount that matches what is considered appropriate sleep in one’s cultural context.”
The researchers also discovered that in all 20 countries, people appeared to be sleeping at least one hour less than what was considered optimal for their culture.
The research underscores the importance of considering cultural context when making recommendations about sleep. It suggests that public health guidelines should be tailored to fit the cultural norms of different populations to promote better health outcomes.
Data for the study came from people in North America, Europe, Asia, Africa and South America.

data.title: A masochist's guide to web development
data.author: sebtron
data.article_summary: 本文是一份关于如何将C语言项目通过Emscripten编译为WebAssembly并在网页上运行的指南，特别适合有C/C++背景但缺乏网页开发经验的开发者。文章详细介绍了从环境设置、编写"Hello World"程序、构建复杂库、多线程处理、Web Workers使用到持久化存储等步骤，强调了过程的复杂性与挑战性。作者提醒，这不是一份传统的网页开发教程，而是侧重将桌面应用移植到网页的技术。读者需要具备基础的HTML和JavaScript知识，并安装Emscripten和简单的web服务器。虽然过程艰难，但可以实现接近原生性能的网页应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：JavaScript开发中的技术选择和挑战，包括模块系统、变量声明、多线程、WebAssembly以及具体开发工具和库的使用。

不同观点：
• [lscharen] 认为使用 `.js` 和 `.mjs` 扩展名都会遇到问题，并基于多年的模块系统使用经验（如CommonsJS、AMD、ESM等）表达了对这一问题的深刻体会。
• [socalgal2] 指出代码中使用 `var` 而不是 `let` 或 `const` 可能引发问题，因为 `var` 的函数作用域特性容易导致错误。此外，讨论了将原生应用移植到 web 时可能遇到的平台特定问题，例如快捷键的跨平台兼容性。
• [apatheticonion] 对 web/Node.js 中的多线程处理表示不满，指出 SharedArrayBuffer 在实际应用中几乎不可用，并描述了他们团队在处理大规模内存应用时面临的挑战，以及考虑使用原生代码进行内存管理的解决方案。
• [lerax] 认为 JavaScript 生态系统非常混乱，相比之下选择更传统的方法可能更理智。
• [knallfrosch] 对文章内容表示赞同，并补充了他们团队在使用 Emscripten 和 C++ 构建项目时的额外复杂性，例如使用 WebGPU、shaders 和 WebAudio 等技术。
• [divbzero] 引用 Emscripten 文档说明编译代码在浏览器中运行可以很快，并指出 WebAssembly 的高效性。
• [broken_broken_] 对文章中提到的文件系统处理提出建议，认为可以使用现代浏览器中内置的 SQLite 数据库，并提出是否可以直接在 WebAssembly 中调用 SQLite API 的问题。

补充讨论：
• [wmichelin] 和 [maximevince] 对文章表示简单回应或感谢，未提出技术性意见。
• [udev4096] 对文章中使用端口 48 进行 SSL 提出疑问，可能是对特定技术选择的困惑或好奇。

争议焦点：
• 关于 `var` 变量声明的问题，部分开发者认为应该避免使用 `var`，以减少作用域相关错误，特别是对非JS背景的开发者而言。
• 多线程处理中的 SharedArrayBuffer 实用性和性能问题也是争议的焦点，部分开发者对其在实际项目中的可用性表示怀疑。

总的来说，讨论围绕着JavaScript开发中的技术选择展开，涉及模块系统、变量声明、多线程处理、WebAssembly应用以及具体开发工具和库的使用。

44200895.article_content:
A masochist’s guide to web development
Table of contents
Introduction
Setting things up
Hello world
Intermezzo I: What is WebAssembly?
Building a library
Intermezzo II: JavaScript and the DOM
Loading the library and making it a module
Multithreading
Intermezzo III: Web Workers and Spectre
Don’t block the main thread!
Callback functions
Persistent storage
Closing thoughts
Introduction
I have recently worked on making a web application out of
my latest Rubik’s cube optimal solver
.
This involved building a rather complex C code base (with
multithreading, SIMD, callback functions and whatnot) to
WebAssembly
via
Emscripten
, and writing a minimal amount of
JavaScript and HTML for the frontend.
This whole process was complex, tiring and at times frustrating -
but eventually
it was a success
! Not only
I accomplished my goal, but I have learnt a lot along the way. After
finishing the work, I decided to write down all that I have learnt and
share it with the world with this post.
You may be wondering why one should do such a thing instead of either
rewriting their code base in a more web-friendly language, or distributing
their app using a native GUI framework. The main reason to use WebAssembly
is that it can provide near-native performance (or so they claim) while
running inside a web browser; this gives you all the portability of a
web app without too much of a performance drawback, something that would
not be possible with an interpreted language such as JavaScript.
So, what is this blog post? A tutorial for web development? I am not sure
about this, but if it is, it is definitely not a normal one. As the title
suggests, you should not start from this guide unless you just
love
banging your head against the wall.  If you are looking for a
sane
guide to web development, I strongly advise you head on to the
Mozilla Developer Network tutorials page
and start from there.
But if you are a C or C++ developer looking to port a program or library
to the web, then you are in the right place. With this post I am going
to walk you through the process of building an increasingly complex
library that can run in a web browser.  Make sure you are
sitting comfortably and be ready to sweat, because I am not going to
shy away from the hard stuff and the complicated details.
To follow this tutorial you won’t need much experience with web
development, but some familiarity with HTML and an idea of what JavaScript
will be useful. It will also help to know that you can access your
browser’s JavaScript console and other developer tools by pressing F12,
at least on Firefox or Chrome - but I guess I have literally just taught
you that, if you did not already know it. For all the rest, I’ll make
sure to add many hyperlinks throughout the text, so you can follow them
if something is new to you.
A little disclaimer: although I am a somewhat experienced C developer,
I had very little web development experience before embarking in
this adventure.  If you are a web developer, you may find errors in
this post that are going to make you laugh at my ignorance. If you do,
I’d appreciate it if you could report them to me by sending an email to
sebastiano@tronto.net
!
With this out of the way, let’s get started!
Setting things up
The examples used in this tutorial are all contained in a git repository,
which you can find either on
my git page
or
on github
.
In order to follow them you are going to need:
A working installation of
Emscripten
(which also includes Node.js). Refer to the official website for
installation instructions.
A web server such
darkhttpd
or the Python
http.server
package; the examples will use darkhttpd.
I have only tested all of this on Linux, but everything should work
exactly the same on any UNIX system. If you are a Windows user, you can
either run everything inside
WSL
, or you can try and
adjust the examples to your system - if you choose this second option,
I’ll happily accept patches or pull requests :)
Hello world
Let’s start with the classic Hello World program:
#include <stdio.h>
int main() {
printf("Hello, web!\n");
}
You can compile the code above with
emcc -o index.html hello.c
And if you now start a web server in the current folder, for example with
darkhttpd .
(the dot at the end is important), and open a web browser to
localhost:8080
(or whatever port your web server
uses), you should see something like this:
As you can see, the compiler generated a bunch of extra stuff around
you print statement. You may or may not want this, but for now we can
take it as a convenient way to check that our program works as expected.
There are other ways to run this compiled code. With the command above,
the compiler should have generated for you 3 files:
index.html
- the web page in the screenshot above.
index.wasm
- the actual compiled code of your program; this file contains
WebAssembly bytecode.
index.js
- some JavaScript
glue code
to make it possible for
index.wasm
to actually run in a browser.

-o inde

data.title: Mapping space: Largest map of the universe announced
data.author: giuliomagnifico
data.article_summary:
文章报道了COSMOS国际科学合作项目发布了有史以来最大的宇宙地图——COSMOS-Web场，包含近80万个星系的图像和目录，覆盖了几乎整个宇宙历史。该项目利用詹姆斯·韦伯空间望远镜（JWST）的数据，揭示了从当前宇宙到135亿年前的景象，涵盖约98%的宇宙时间。研究不仅关注早期有趣的星系，还着眼于宇宙早期环境的全貌。

令人惊讶的是，JWST发现了比预期多10倍的星系，以及哈勃望远镜无法看到的超大质量黑洞。此外，JWST的数据还挑战了现有的宇宙学模型，因早期宇宙产生的光量远超预期。尽管新发现解答了许多问题，但也引发了更多未解之谜，例如暗物质和早期宇宙物理。

该项目的数据已向公众开放，旨在促进全球天文学家共同探索宇宙的演化。COSMOS合作项目还致力于将顶尖望远镜的数据民主化，使其更广泛地被使用。

M. Franco / C. Casey / COSMOS-Web collaboration
Six images of galaxies taken from nearly 800,000, from upper left to lower right: the present-day universe, and 3, 4, 8, 9 and 10 billion years ago
Science + Technology
June 5, 2025
Mapping space: Largest map of the universe announced
Sonia Fernandez
In the name of open science, the multinational scientific collaboration COSMOS on Thursday has released the data behind the largest map of the universe. Called the COSMOS-Web field, the project, with data collected by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), consists of all the imaging and a catalog of nearly 800,000 galaxies spanning nearly all of cosmic time. And it’s been challenging existing notions of the infant universe.
“Our goal was to construct this deep field of space on a physical scale that far exceeded anything that had been done before,” said UC Santa Barbara
physics
professor
Caitlin Casey
, who co-leads the COSMOS collaboration with Jeyhan Kartaltepe of the Rochester Institute of Technology. “If you had a printout of the Hubble Ultra Deep Field on a standard piece of paper,” she said, referring to the iconic view of nearly 10,000 galaxies released by NASA in 2004, “our image would be slightly larger than a 13-foot by 13-foot-wide mural, at the same depth. So it’s really strikingly large.”
An animated zoom-out from the center of the COSMOS-Web field to a full-size comparison between COSMOS-Web and the Hubble Ultra Deep Field
The COSMOS-Web composite image reaches back about 13.5 billion years; according to NASA, the universe is about 13.8 billion years old, give or take one hundred million years. That covers about 98% of all cosmic time. The objective for the researchers was not just to see some of the most interesting galaxies at the beginning of time but also to see the wider view of cosmic environments that existed during the early universe, during the formation of the first stars, galaxies and black holes.
“The cosmos is organized in dense regions and voids,” Casey explained. “And we wanted to go beyond finding the most distant galaxies; we wanted to get that broader context of where they lived.”
A 'big surprise'
And what a cosmic neighborhood it turned out to be. Before JWST turned on, Casey said, she and fellow astronomers made their best predictions about how many more galaxies the space telescope would be able to see, given its 6.5 meter (21 foot) diameter light-collecting primary mirror, about six times larger than Hubble’s 2.4 meter (7 foot, 10 in) diameter mirror. The best measurements from Hubble suggested that galaxies within the first 500 million years would be incredibly rare, she said.
“It makes sense — the Big Bang happens and things take time to gravitationally collapse and form, and for stars to turn on. There’s a timescale associated with that,” Casey explained. “And the big surprise is that with JWST, we see roughly 10 times more galaxies than expected at these incredible distances. We’re also seeing supermassive black holes that are not even visible with Hubble.” And they’re not just seeing more, they’re seeing different types of galaxies and black holes, she added.
“Since the telescope turned on we’ve been wondering ‘Are these JWST datasets breaking the cosmological model? Because the universe was producing too much light too early; it had only about 400 million years to form something like a billion solar masses of stars. We just do not know how to make that happen."
'Lots of unanswered questions'
While the COSMOS-Web images and catalog answer many questions astronomers have had about the early universe, they also spark more questions.
“Since the telescope turned on we’ve been wondering ‘Are these JWST datasets breaking the cosmological model? Because the universe was producing too much light too early; it had only about 400 million years to form something like a billion solar masses of stars. We just do not know how to make that happen,” Casey said. “So, lots of details to unpack, and lots of unanswered questions.”
In releasing the data to the public, the hope is that other astronomers from all over the world will use it to, among other things, further refine our understanding of how the early universe was populated and how everything evolved to the present day. The dataset may also provide clues to other outstanding mysteries of the cosmos, such as dark matter and physics of the early universe that may be different from what we know today.
“A big part of this project is the democratization of science and making tools and data from the best telescopes accessible to the broader community,” Casey said. The data was made public almost immediately after it was gathered, but only in its raw form, useful only to those with the specialized technical knowledge and the supercomputer access to process and interpret it. 这篇文章简要介绍了高斯求积法中的切比雪夫-高斯求积法，用于计算定积分。切比雪夫-高斯求积法利用切比雪夫多项式的根作为节点，这些节点在区间边缘分布更密集，有助于减小多项式拟合时的震荡误差（如龙格现象）。与基本数值积分方法相比，高斯求积法在相同的节点数下可以处理更高阶的多项式，从而提高积分精度。

文章还讨论了如何将任意区间和函数形式转换为适合切比雪夫-高斯求积法的形式。通过适当的变换，可以将积分区间从$$a, b$$映射到$$[-1, 1]$$，并调整函数形式以适应求积公式。文章最后提到使用交互式笔记本工具（marimo notebook）来演示该方法，并提供了代码示例供读者尝试。

data.title: The last six months in LLMs, illustrated by pelicans on bicycles
data.author: swyx
data.article_summary: Simon Willison在2025年6月6日的博客中总结了大型语言模型（LLM）在过去六个月的进展。他在三届AI Engineer World’s Fair上发表了演讲，这次重点讨论了过去六个月LLM的快速发展。由于新模型发布频繁，他强调评估和选择适合模型的难度。他通过让模型生成“鹈鹕骑自行车”的SVG图像来测试它们的能力，发现即使对于人类来说，这也是一个困难的任务。Willison指出，2024年12月Meta发布的Llama 3.3 70B模型是他能在自己笔记本上运行的最强模型，而中国AI实验室DeepSeek在圣诞节发布的开放权重模型成为了当时的最佳开放模型。2025年1月27日，DeepSeek再次发布R1推理模型，其竞争力引发了市场反应，导致NVIDIA市值蒸发6000亿美元。Willison认为，鹈鹕骑自行车的测试显示了模型的局限性和进步。

Simon Willison’s Weblog
Subscribe
The last six months in LLMs, illustrated by pelicans on bicycles
6th June 2025
I presented an invited keynote at the
AI Engineer World’s Fair
in San Francisco this week. This is my third time speaking at the event—here are my talks from
October 2023
and
June 2024
. My topic this time was “The last six months in LLMs”—originally planned as the last year, but so much has happened that I had to reduce my scope!
You can watch the talk
on the AI Engineer YouTube channel
. Below is a full annotated transcript of the talk and accompanying slides, plus additional links to related articles and resources.
#
I originally pitched this session as “The last year in LLMs”. With hindsight that was foolish—the space has been accelerating to the point that even covering the last six months is a tall order!
Thankfully almost all of the noteworthy models we are using today were released within the last six months. I’ve counted over 30 models from that time period that are significant enough that people working in this space should at least be aware of them.
With so many great models out there, the classic problem remains how to evaluate them and figure out which ones work best.
There are plenty of benchmarks full of numbers. I don’t get much value out of those numbers.
There are leaderboards, but I’ve been
losing some trust
in those recently.
Everyone needs their own benchmark. So I’ve been increasingly leaning on my own, which started as a joke but is beginning to show itself to actually be a little bit useful!
#
I ask them to generate
an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle
.
I’m running this against text output LLMs. They shouldn’t be able to draw anything at all.
But they can generate code... and SVG is code.
This is also an unreasonably difficult test for them. Drawing bicycles is really hard! Try it yourself now, without a photo: most people find it difficult to remember the exact orientation of the frame.
Pelicans are glorious birds but they’re also pretty difficult to draw.
Most importantly:
pelicans can’t ride bicycles
. They’re the wrong shape!
#
A fun thing about SVG is that it supports comments, and LLMs almost universally include comments in their attempts. This means you get a better idea of what they were
trying
to achieve.
#
Let’s start with December 2024,
which was
a lot
.
#
At the start of November Amazon released the first three of their
Nova models
. These haven’t made many waves yet but are notable because they handle 1 million tokens of input and feel competitive with the less expensive of Google’s Gemini family. The Nova models are also
really cheap
—
nova-micro
is the cheapest model I currently track on my
llm-prices.com
table.
They’re not great at drawing pelicans.
#
The most exciting model release in December was Llama 3.3 70B from Meta—the final model in their Llama 3 series.
The B stands for billion—it’s the number of parameters. I’ve got 64GB of RAM on my three year old M2 MacBook Pro, and my rule of thumb is that 70B is about the largest size I can run.
At the time, this was clearly the best model I had ever managed to run on own laptop. I wrote about this in
I can now run a GPT-4 class model on my laptop
.
Meta themselves claim that this model has similar performance to their much larger Llama 3.1 405B.
I never thought I’d be able to run something that felt as capable as early 2023 GPT-4 on my own hardware without some
serious
upgrades, but here it was.
It does use up all of my memory, so I can’t run anything else at the same time.
#
Then on Christmas day the Chinese AI lab DeepSeek
dropped a huge open weight model
on Hugging Face, with no documentation at all. A real drop-the-mic moment.
As people started to try it out it became apparent that it was probably the best available open weights model.
In the paper
that followed the day after
they claimed training time of 2,788,000 H800 GPU hours, producing an estimated cost of $5,576,000.
That’s notable because I would have expected a model of this size to cost 10 to 100 times more.
#
January the 27th was an exciting day: DeepSeek struck again! This time with the open weights release of their R1 reasoning model, competitive with OpenAI’s o1.
#
Maybe because they didn’t release this one in Christmas Day, people actually took notice. The resulting stock market dive wiped $600 billion from NVIDIA’s valuation, which I believe is a record drop for a single company.
It turns out trade restrictions on the best GPUs weren’t going to stop the Chinese labs from finding new optimizations for training great models.
#
Here’s the pelican on the bicycle that crashed the stock market. It’s the best we have seen so far: clearly a bicycle and there’s a bird that could almost be described as looking a bit like a pelican. It’s not riding the bicycle though.
#
My favorite model release from January was another local model,
Mistral Small 3
. It’s 24B which means I can run it in my laptop using less than 20GB of RAM, leaving enough for me to

data.title: A look at Cloudflare's AI-coded OAuth library
data.author: itsadok
data.article_summary: CloudFlare的新OAuth提供者库主要借助Anthropic的Claude大语言模型编写，并经过CloudFlare工程师的严格审查，确保安全性和合规性。尽管代码整体结构良好，但测试不够全面，尤其在安全性测试方面有所欠缺。代码中存在一些可疑的选择，比如广泛允许CORS头，但这是人为决定而非Claude的建议。此外，代码缺乏标准的安全头配置，比如未设置"X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff"和HTTP严格传输安全。还有一些对OAuth规范不熟悉的迹象，例如错误地实现了OAuth 2.1中已移除的隐式授权。尽管如此，Claude在某些方面仍提供了有价值的帮助，但整体仍需更多人工审查和改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在编程中的应用及其潜在问题和局限性

不同观点：
• afro88认为，使用LLM时需要具备足够的知识才能有效交互。经验丰富的工程师能发现LLM输出的问题，但对于不熟悉相关领域的人来说，可能会忽略一些关键错误。因此，使用LLM的效率提升依赖于用户的审查能力和领导力。
• sarchertech分享了使用AI辅助编写代码的实际经验，认为AI在一次性项目和不熟悉的语言上能显著提升效率，但在复杂和长期项目中提升有限。同时，担忧中级技术人员可能因依赖AI而忽视潜在的细微错误，进而对代码质量产生负面影响。
• aiono强调了人类在代码审查中的认知偏见，指出自己编写代码更能发现潜在问题。通过编写工具的学习效果优于仅阅读相关材料。
• HocusLocus建议通过AI引入和修复漏洞的游戏化方法来提高代码安全性。
• max2he对将提示提交到Git仓库的做法表示好奇，并质疑其是否会成为普遍接受的做法。
• epolanski怀疑“LLM编写”可能是一种吸引关注和获得免费审查的策略，同时追求其他目标如AI效率展示和实验。
• kentonv作为库的作者回应了一些批评，解释了代码设计背后的考虑，并指出如果知道代码会受到如此多关注，可能会更仔细地审查代码。
• dweekly提出使用不同模型的代理来互相审查和测试代码，以捕捉一些简单的错误，但承认不能替代人类的参与。
• roxolotl担心LLM会冻结社会知识，因为模型可能依赖于过时或错误的信息源。
• menzoic将LLM比作电动工具，强调理解架构和正确应用技术的重要性。
• djoldman通过个人经验说明OAuth实现中的复杂性和潜在问题。
• kcatskcolbdi关注LLM输出中的明显错误和开发人员对LLM输出的过度依赖。
• OutOfHere描述了一种通过多次迭代和多个LLM审查规格文档和代码的方法，以解决大部分专业知识问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是LLM生成代码的可靠性和安全性，尤其是中级技术人员可能因依赖AI而引入错误。
• 另一个讨论点是LLM对代码质量和知识发展的长期影响，包括对中级技术人员和初级到高级工程师培养的影响。
• 使用多个LLM进行代码审查和测试的方法被提出作为提高代码质量的一种潜在策略。
• 对于将提示提交到Git仓库的做法是否会被广泛接受，存在疑问和讨论。

这些观点共同描绘了LLM在编程应用中的潜力和挑战，强调了人类审查和专业知识在确保代码质量方面的重要作用。

data.title: The Illusion of Thinking: Strengths and Limitations of Reasoning Models
data.author: sunshinerag
data.article_summary: 《The Illusion of Thinking》一文探讨了前沿语言模型中的大型推理模型（LRMs）在处理复杂问题时的优势和局限。尽管LRMs在推理任务中表现出色，但其基本能力、扩展性及局限尚未完全理解。传统评估主要关注最终答案的准确性，而忽略了推理过程的质量。本文通过可控的 puzzle 环境系统地分析了LRMs的性能，发现其在超过一定复杂度后准确率大幅下降，且推理努力在达到某一复杂度后反而减少。比较LRMs与标准LLMs，本文识别出三种性能模式：低复杂度任务中标准模型表现更好，中等复杂度任务中LRMs有优势，高复杂度任务中两者均失效。研究还揭示LRMs在精确计算和一致性推理方面存在不足，提出了对其真正推理能力的质疑。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：当前人工智能（AGI）的推理能力及其局限性

不同观点：
• 观点一：当前的“推理”模型在面对复杂问题时会遭遇准确性崩溃。Piskov认为，无论增加多少计算能力，这些模型在解决更难的问题时都会失败，表明我们离实现通用人工智能（AGI）还有很长的路。他引用了Apple研究人员的实验结果，这些实验显示模型在处理复杂逻辑问题时表现不佳，暗示当前的“推理”突破可能遇到了无法通过增加数据或计算能力解决的根本性障碍。

• 观点二：研究表明模型可能只是依赖于记忆而非真正的推理能力。Piskov提到的实验中，模型能够在Tower of Hanoi puzzle中处理100+步，但在River Crossing puzzle中却仅能处理4步。这表明模型可能只是通过训练数据记住了特定类型问题的解决方案，而并非具备普遍的逻辑推理能力。

补充讨论：
• 实验设计的重要性：Apple研究人员选择使用可控的 puzzle 环境，以避免数据污染，并能够精确控制问题的复杂性。这种设计能够揭示模型在不同复杂度问题上的真实表现，帮助识别模型的局限性。

• 争议焦点：当前“推理”模型的实际能力与AGI的距离。一部分人可能认为现有的模型进展显著，距离AGI不远；而另一部分人，如Piskov，则认为模型在复杂问题上的表现揭示了其根本性局限，距离AGI还有很大差距。

• 论据和例子：Piskov引用了具体实验结果（如模型在不同puzzle中的表现）来支持其观点，强调了模型在需要纯逻辑推理的任务中表现不佳，这为讨论提供了实证基础。

总结来看，讨论围绕当前AI模型的推理能力及其在复杂问题上的表现展开，不同观点聚焦于这些模型是否真正接近AGI，以及它们是否具备真正的推理能力，还是仅仅依赖于记忆。

The Illusion of Thinking: Understanding the Strengths and Limitations of Reasoning Models via the Lens of Problem Complexity
Authors
Parshin Shojaee*â , Iman Mirzadeh*, Keivan Alizadeh, Maxwell Horton, Samy Bengio, Mehrdad Farajtabar
View publication
Copy Bibtex
Recent generations of frontier language models have introduced Large Reasoning Models
(LRMs) that generate detailed thinking processes before providing answers. While these models
demonstrate improved performance on reasoning benchmarks, their fundamental capabilities, scal-
ing properties, and limitations remain insufficiently understood. Current evaluations primarily fo-
cus on established mathematical and coding benchmarks, emphasizing final answer accuracy. How-
ever, this evaluation paradigm often suffers from data contamination and does not provide insights
into the reasoning tracesâ structure and quality. In this work, we systematically investigate these
gaps with the help of controllable puzzle environments that allow precise manipulation of composi-
tional complexity while maintaining consistent logical structures. This setup enables the analysis
of not only final answers but also the internal reasoning traces, offering insights into how LRMs
âthinkâ. Through extensive experimentation across diverse puzzles, we show that frontier LRMs
face a complete accuracy collapse beyond certain complexities. Moreover, they exhibit a counter-
intuitive scaling limit: their reasoning effort increases with problem complexity up to a point, then
declines despite having an adequate token budget. By comparing LRMs with their standard LLM
counterparts under equivalent inference compute, we identify three performance regimes: (1) low-
complexity tasks where standard models surprisingly outperform LRMs, (2) medium-complexity
tasks where additional thinking in LRMs demonstrates advantage, and (3) high-complexity tasks
where both models experience complete collapse. We found that LRMs have limitations in exact
computation: they fail to use explicit algorithms and reason inconsistently across puzzles. We
also investigate the reasoning traces in more depth, studying the patterns of explored solutions
and analyzing the modelsâ computational behavior, shedding light on their strengths, limitations,
and ultimately raising crucial questions about their true reasoning capabilities.
*Equal contribution.

data.title: Focus and Context and LLMs
data.author: tarasglek
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了大语言模型（LLM）在软件工程任务中的应用，特别是复杂编码任务的完成能力。作者指出，尽管LLM能够完成一些人类工程师难以应对的编码任务，但这种能力高度依赖于提供的上下文质量和严格的算法监督。文章批评了当前对“代理编码”工具的过度炒作，认为这些工具无法如宣传那样自动生成大量有用的软件。作者通过一个HTTP/2服务器项目的例子说明，LLM在编写代码时需要大量人工干预和精细的上下文管理，且生产JSON等格式时表现不佳。最终，作者强调，LLM的有效性取决于输入的上下文质量，目前仅在优秀工程师手中才能展现出真正 impressive 的结果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：无代码或少代码开发复杂软件的可行性以及AI在代码调试和生成中的表现

不同观点：
• **mharrison**：认为无需编码或仅需少量编码即可构建复杂软件，并举例说明某YouTube视频中，作者在一小时内构建了一个绘图应用。他还提到AI（如o3）在处理大型代码模块时表现出色，可以进行调试并优化代码。然而，在使用某些CLI或IDE的agent模式时，AI的表现明显下降，容易被工具调用干扰。

• **summarity**：支持mharrison的观点，分享个人经验表明AI在处理大型代码和复杂调试任务时有效，如调试Nim宏和优化图形程序。但他也指出，AI在使用工具或进入agent模式时表现不佳，容易混乱。他认为在提供过多工具和保持高效提示之间需要找到平衡。

• **emorning3**：认为文章的核心是“上下文至关重要”，并强调人类助理的必要性。他的观点更倾向于AI在无代码开发中的辅助角色，而不是完全替代人类。

• **quantum_state**：简洁地指出“上下文是一切”，暗示上下文在AI处理任务中的重要性，但没有深入讨论无代码开发的具体表现。

补充讨论：
• AI在不同环境和工具下的性能变化是争议的焦点，尤其是mharrison和summarity提到的agent模式下的表现问题。
• 人类在无代码或少代码开发中的角色仍然不可或缺，这与AI的技术局限性形成对比。
• 提示工程（prompt engineering）和工具调用对AI表现的影响是另一个值得注意的讨论点。

44215726.article_content:
Table of Contents
LLMs Can Complete Hard Software Engineering Tasks.
Context is everything
I decided to write down some thoughts on
agentic coding
and why it’s a very hyped wrong turn.
Let me start with some background on my LLM experience. I adopted LLMs into my work in Aug 2020. I was sold when I saw that GPT-3 could generate usable SQL statements. Something that used to take 4-8 hours of RTFMing, now took 15min. I have since worked on
chatcraft.org
, various RAG frameworks, etc. I use
aider
heavily for work, frequently switch models, have been
struggling
with tool calling since before MCP as even an idea.
LLMs Can Complete Hard Software Engineering Tasks.
#
According to the Internet hive mind agentic coding tools can complete multiple implementations of complete software
(write code this way or FOMO). This
video
is a perfect example (if this were true we would be drowning in useful software). “ADHD software agents on meth” is how I would describe that approach to software engineering.
I would double down on influencer claims and say that LLM-enabled tools can complete software that a large fraction of currently employed engineers would fail at
However so far I’m only aware of 1 such end-to-end AI-written project:
HTTP/2 server
(
blog post
). This is the single most impressive code-gen project I’ve seen so far. I did not think this was possible yet.
Highlights from: Building a 100% LLM-written, standards-compliant HTTP 2.0 server from scratch with Gemini 2.5 Pro
A ridiculous amount of work went into feeding the LLM correct context
Author micromanaged LLM workflow to keep it progressing. LLMs would get stuck, author would split up tests, devised an algo for changing LLM context when LLM got stuck, devised a files-as-units-of-work strategy, etc
It would have been impossible to complete the test by relying on tool calling. This matches experience in aider
blog
. That’s ironic because tool calling is the unreliable foundation of current agentic hype. Another interesting thing is that producing JSON is very difficult for LLMs. Often ad-hoc formats that LLMs were not tuned for work better.
It took days just to stream all the API calls (Google is 2-4x faster than Anthropic) and weeks to get completed software
So yes, LLMs can write code, but instead of being free agents, they can only write software under intense algorithmic supervision by extremely stubborn software engineers. The irony is that under such tight controls even junior human software writers might succeed at this task.
Context is everything
#
The output produced by an LLM is only as good as the context fed into it (including the original question). This is a hard unsolved problem. Current agentic programming is similar (but much worse) to the
genetic algorithm
hype I remember for the 90s. Yes, brute-force works, but it’s often too expensive of a solution.
I think until we come up with a better way to curate context for LLMs, they will only be truly impressive in the hands of exceptional software engineers (
Kenton
and
Sean
are also incredible communicators).
In the meantime continue expecting mediocre results from mediocre people feeding LLMs mediocre context.

• **[throwaway71271]** 认为LLM的能力令人困惑，因为它们使用类似于人类的语言，但其内部运作机制却与人类思维不同。尽管理解其技术原理，但其语言能力看似像魔法。他强调需要更多努力来理解如何使用这些模型并构建超越单一模块的系统。

• **[stephc_int13]** 指出人类语言作为认知工具的不足，认为LLM/LRM依赖语言流利度和知识检索来模拟智能，但这并不能代表真正的强认知能力。人类容易被LLM/LRM的表现所迷惑，因为我们也常用语言能力作为衡量智力的标准。

• **[curious_cat_163]** 对复杂任务的性能划分表示兴趣，并建议将这种划分与经济价值联系起来。他认为除了谜题评估外，还需要更复杂的任务控制和评估。

• **[antics]** 提出模型的“全知但愚钝”特性，并质疑这种特性是否会持续下去。他认为AI最大化主义者和怀疑论者对此有不同看法，且目前没有令人信服的量化方法来解决这一争议。

• **[gwd]** 支持模型在复杂性超过某一阈值时表现崩溃的观点，并以编码为例说明问题复杂性管理的重要性。

• **[actinium226]** 调侃AI发展的“Gartner hype cycle”，暗示对AGI即将到来的期望过于乐观。

• **[jbentley1]** 质疑Apple在AI方面的研发策略，暗示其可能因为失败而转向不重视AI的立场。

• **[teleforce]** 认为LLM/LRM需要逻辑、优化和约束编程等方法的帮助，以实现智能自动化，并提供相关资源链接。

• **[thomasahle]** 认为如果允许LLM编写代码，很多复杂问题可以被完美解决，质疑LLM在计算能力上的局限性是否真的显著。

• **[JusticeJuice]** 赞同LLM在简单任务上表现最佳，LRM在中等复杂任务上表现最佳，而在真正复杂任务上均失败的观点。

• **[ksec]** 对AI/LLM/LRM的发展进度表示怀疑，认为这些技术仍停留在模式匹配阶段，缺乏真正的推理能力，并将其与“ illusion of thinking”联系起来。

• **[kamranjon]** 指出两个有趣的发现：即使在提示中给出解决方案，推理模型仍需要相同步骤才能找到可行方案；需要大量token才能使推理模型显著优于非推理模型。

• **[nialv7]** 批评论文中未明确定义关键术语如“推理”和“通用化”，并挑战人类是否具备论文中所定义的通用化推理能力。

补充讨论：
• **[mitch_said]** 制作了思维导图以帮助理解原始论文，显示出对复杂内容进行简化理解的努力。

• **[danck]** 对LRM在复杂任务中自我纠正能力的局限性表示关注，并质疑是否仅通过增加token预算就能解决这一问题。

争议焦点：
• LLM/LRM是否具备真正的推理能力，或仅为高级模式匹配工具。
• 这些模型在复杂任务中的表现崩溃是否仅为规模问题，能否通过增加资源解决。
• 如何定义和评估推理和通用化能力，以及人类是否具备这些能力。

data.title: Why not use DNS over HTTPS (DoH)?
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了DNS over HTTPS（DoH）的争议。DoH旨在通过HTTPS加密DNS查询，以保护用户隐私，但批评者指出，它实际上将所有查询集中到一个DNS提供商（如Cloudflare）手中，使其成为唯一的"窥探者"。文章认为，DoH增加了不必要的复杂性，可能引入安全漏洞，且Cloudflare作为商业公司可能利用数据牟利。作者建议拒绝使用DoH，并在Firefox中设置`network.trr.mode`为5来禁用它。作为替代，文章推荐使用DNS over TLS（DoT），这是一种不依赖HTTP的加密方式。作者支持DNS现代化，但反对DoH作为解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DNS over HTTPS（DoH）的优缺点及替代方案

不同观点：
• **支持DoH**：
   - DoH能有效对抗ISP对DNS流量的过滤，尤其是对那些不合理屏蔽网站的ISP（例如[dabacaba]）。
   - 相比于将DNS查询暴露给ISP，使用像Cloudflare这样更可信的公司可以提高隐私保护（例如[om8], [creata]）。
   - DoH的流量伪装特性使得它更难被封锁，相比DNS over UDP有更好的抗审查能力（例如[sudahtigabulan]）。

• **质疑DoH**：
   - DoH将所有查询集中到一个提供商（如Cloudflare），虽然防止了中间人攻击，但将数据集中在一个可信实体手中并不理想（例如[xrmagnum], [orbital-decay]）。
   - DoH可能带来新的安全复杂性，并且并不是解决DNS隐私问题的唯一方法（例如[elashri], [conradev]）。
   - 有人认为DoH会削弱用户对DNS的控制，例如Brave浏览器强制启用DoH导致用户无法完全禁用（例如[ddtaylor]）。

• **DoH与DoT的对比**：
   - **支持DoT**：DoT使用TLS加密，不依赖HTTP协议，避免了DoH的"滥用HTTP"问题，同时也能提供类似的隐私保护（例如[conradev], [sudahtigabulan]）。
   - **DoT的局限性**：DoT更容易被ISP封锁，不如DoH那样能伪装成普通HTTPS流量（例如[sudahtigabulan]）。

• **自建DNS基础设施**：
   - 自建DNS服务器可以避免将查询交给不信任的第三方，同时还能避免审查和限制，但需要投入时间和资金（例如[exiguus], [elashri]）。
   - 推荐的工具包括dnsdist、bind和unbound等，可以实现DNS over TLS和DoH（例如[exiguus]）。

补充讨论：
• **关于信任问题**：有评论指出，无论使用DoH还是DoT，最终都需要信任某个实体来处理DNS查询，除非完全使用像Tor这样的工具（例如[elashri], [mixdup]）。
• **OHAI和DNSCrypt**：一些评论提到OHAI（Oblivious HTTP）和DNSCrypt作为DoH的替代或补充方案，提供了更多的隐私保护选项（例如[toomim], [creatonez]）。
• **Cloudflare与ISP的信任对比**：部分评论认为，Cloudflare等大公司比本地ISP更值得信任，特别是在互联网受国家严格控制的地方（例如[om8], [ahmetozer]）。

44215608.article_content:
BSDHowTo.ch
How To...
Why not..?
Scripts
Patches
Why not use DNS over HTTPS (DoH)?
Last update: 2018-10-26
tl;dr
DoH is not about protecting your DNS queries from peepers. That is a
big lie. It is about making sure only one peeper can see all of your
queries.
Refuse to use it today: Open about:config in Firefox and set
network.trr.mode
to
5
. This will prevent Firefox from using DoH
under all circumstances.
What is DNS over HTTPS (DoH)?
DNS over HTTPS is described in
RFC 8484
as a way perform DNS by wrapping it in HTTP and additionally encrypt the
data using TLS.
Advocates of DoH stress that the transport encryption protects your DNS
queries from peepers like your ISP or your network admin at work.
Adversaries critic that all DNS queries are directed to single DNS
provider who becomes the one known peeper.
The basic idea
The basic idea behind new developments like DoH is to protect your DNS
queries from peepers by implementing transport encryption. The same type
of transport encryption that protects many other application protocols
like HTTP and SMTP.
This is a very good idea because DNS queries in clear text contain very
interesting meta data about the sites you communicate with over the
Internet. This can be useful information for any kind of bad guy, be it
the NSA or the cyber-criminal.
DoH encrypts, so it must be a good thing
The public didn't care about this RFC until Mozilla announced that they
implement this new protocol in Firefox for broad field testing in
collaboration with Cloudflare. The first reactions to this were: “DNS
gets encryption? This must be good thing.“ But slowly people started to
realize what the collaboration between Mozilla and Cloudflare really
means: Cloudflare gets all your DNS queries.
But Cloudflare has a data protection policy
So what? Cloudflare is a commercial company. And commercial companies,
by definition, must earn money. How does a modern company in the IT
business earn money? By selling data.
Is there an alternative way?
Yes, there is. It is called DNS over TLS and is specified as a proposed
standard in
RFC 7858
.  This
provides transport encryption to DNS without abusing HTTP as transport
protocol.
Why are you against changes in DNS?
I'm not. The DNS needs modernization. The DNS needs security features
that prevent the peepers from reading your DNS traffic. I'm all in for
it. But DoH is NOT the answer to this.
But the protocol itself is a good idea
No, it is not. Abusing HTTP as a transport protocol for DNS data adds a
unneeded complexity to the protocol. You must add a HTTP module to all
DNS servers or interact with a separated HTTP server on the same system
in order to support DoH. That is a lot of code which can contain a lot
of bugs and security flaws. Complexity is the enemy of security.

data.title: Workhorse LLMs: Why Open Source Models Dominate Closed Source for Batch Tasks
data.author: cmogni1
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了在批处理任务中，开源大语言模型（LLM）相比闭源模型（如GPT、Claude、Gemini）的优势。尽管闭源模型在高端智能任务中仍占主导，但对于大多数常见的低至中等复杂度任务（如分类、摘要、数据提取等），开源模型表现相当甚至更好，且成本更低。文章通过对比工作模型（workhorse models）的性能和成本，指出在批量任务中使用开源模型（如Qwen、DeepSeek）可以显著节省开支，特别是在使用批量推理服务时。文章还提供了选择开源模型的指南和成本节省预期。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同编码模型的成本与性能评估

不同观点：
• jbellis 认为作者的分析仅适合初步评估，有些场景下即使成本低，模型性能若低于某个“智能底线”，则再便宜也无用。他指出Grok 3 mini和DeepSeek V3分别是考虑是否在意供应商训练需求时最值得尝试的廉价模型。他还提到作者的评估方法通过将人工智能分析分数除以混合每token成本来进行，这种方法可能不准确，尤其是当去掉极便宜的开源模型（如4B OSS模型）的高分结果后，其他模型明显不如Flash 2.0和2.5。他特别指出Haiku模型在2025年不应再被使用。

• delichon 则认为选择模型应更具情境性，希望有一个更简化的选择机制，如"<dumber>"和"<smarter>"按钮，按$/M tokens为单位进行选择。他建议可以先使用快速、低成本的模型处理简单任务，当任务复杂时再切换到更智能但较慢的模型。

• ramesh31 表示Flash模型目前价格极为低廉，因此自托管模型（自己 hosting）不太划算，除非是处理敏感数据的情况下。

补充讨论：
• jbellis 特别提到Grok 3 mini在特定领域任务（如编码）中可能表现更好，并对OpenAI mini模型的使用场景表示质疑。
• delichon 强调了模型选择的上下文依赖性和用户对不同任务的性能需求变化。
• ramesh31 则关注在成本与隐私（敏感数据）之间的权衡，认为Flash模型的低成本使其在大多数情况下成为优选。

争议焦点：
• jbellis 和 ramesh31 对自托管模型的必要性存在不同看法。jbellis 认为某些开源模型在特定任务中仍有价值，而ramesh31 则认为除非涉及敏感数据，否则Flash的低成本使其成为更优选择。
• jbellis 和 delichon 的讨论反映了对模型选择简化机制的需求与复杂任务中性能要求的权衡。

Workhorse LLMs: Why Open Source Models Dominate Closed Source for Batch Tasks
Sutro Team
Jun 6, 2025
As LLMs become more prolific, weâve noticed that teams still reach for closed sourced models like GPT, Claude, and Gemini for nearly every task. While this may have been the right call a year ago, teams today are unknowingly missing out on huge cost savings and performance gains by not considering open source alternatives.
It is true that at the frontier of intelligence, the most powerful closed source LLMs dominate their open source counterparts. However, many common tasks for LLMs donât require PhD level reasoning. Instead, they require a workhorse LLM: something thatâs reliable for low-to-medium difficulty tasks â things like classification, summarization, and data extraction.
Not only are there suitable replacements for closed source workhorses like GPT-4o-mini, but the equivalent replacements are often less expensive
and
more intelligent. When latency isnât an issue, open source models have an even larger edge for cost savings if running jobs in bulk through a batch inference provider like Sutro.
In this guide, we compare the performance and cost of workhorse models. After the analysis, we provide a handy conversion chart that helps you pick the best open source replacement for the closed source models you may have used along with the cost savings you should expect by making the switch.
How Do Open Source LLMs Stack Up Against Closed Source LLMs?
A common question organizations ask us is how the cost and performance of open source models stack up against closed source models. To answer this question, itâs best to divide the field into two categories: frontier models and workhorse models.
Frontier models are the biggest, most capable models. They promise emergent capabilities, generalization across tasks, and the ability to handle complex context and instructions.
At the frontier, closed source models like Claude Opus 4.0, OpenAIâs o3 model, and Gemini 2.5 Pro dominate. However, open source models like Qwen 3 235B-A22B and DeepSeek R1 (and the to-be-released R2) are closing the gap quickly.
The closed providers also provide smaller, less-expensive models. These include GPT-4o mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Claude Haiku 3.5. Many companies choose to adopt these models to save on costs when running tasks that require less general reasoning capabilities.  We refer to these as âworkhorseâ models, and believe that for this class of model open-source dominates.
Workhorse models are extremely adept at most common business tasks, including:
Structured Extraction:
Turning free form-text or images into JSON format and analytics-ready datasets.
Summarizing Text:
Turning large documents or conversations into bullet points or summaries.
Answering Questions:
Doing Q&A that doesnât require complex reasoning on your documents.
Sentiment Analysis:
Determining how positive, negative, or neutral a given text is.
Generating Synthetic Data:
Creating datasets from scratch to power fine-tuning or improving RAG systems.
Data Extraction And Organization:
Finding and extracting particular pieces of information from unstructured text.
Classification:
Sorting text into categories specific to your applications.
Running Evals:
Evaluating the robustness of your prompts using techniques like LLM-as-a-judge and metric scoring.
Most organizations already use models like GPT-4o-mini and Gemini 2.5 Flash to do these tasks to speed up inference and keep costs low. As we demonstrate below, equivalent open source LLMs can get you the same or better performance, sometimes with huge cost savings, especially if using a batch API like Sutro.
How Open Source LLMs For Common Business Tasks Stack Up
Figuring out how well an LLM performs is tricky. Most model creators game benchmarks by training for the test and testing using prompts that are carefully crafted to perform well. Nonetheless, because model providers are all trying to game the system in similar ways, benchmarks still give us a heuristic for
relative
capabilities.
To determine which workhorse open source models are likely a good replacement performance and cost wise for closed source models you have probably used, we will use Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index. The Intelligence Index is a weighted average of benchmarks across many tasks. Using this lets us not overweight any one benchmark and helps us get the heuristic we are looking for.
Additionally, we pulled together the average cost per token for common workhorse tasks. We used a 10:1 blended ratio of input-to-output tokens for non-thinking models, which we calculated from internal metrics. For models with thinking mode, we budgeted 2k thinking tokens, adjusting the blended ratio to 3:2.

• ramesh31 表示Flash模型目前价格极为低廉，因此自托管模型（自己 hosting）不太划算，除非是处理敏感数据的情况下。

data.title: Apple Is on Defense at WWDC
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 苹果公司在2025年WWDC上面临压力。与前几年不同，2023年推出的Vision Pro头戴设备因销售不佳而减产，可以在eBay上以大幅折扣购买。2024年的人工智能（AI）更新也被指令人失望，Siri的重大升级被推迟，甚至可能多年无法实现。此外，苹果还面临法律问题，因未遵循法院命令让开发者添加外部购买链接，被法官严厉批评，甚至可能面临刑事藐视法庭的诉讼。在欧盟，苹果因违反反垄断法被罚款，同时《Fortnite》重回App Store。再加上特朗普威胁对苹果产品加征关税，公司内外压力倍增。作者希望在WWDC上看到蒂姆·库克承认公司近期的失误，而不是继续展示过度宣传但未实现的技术。然而，迹象表明苹果可能仍会选择保持自信姿态，掩饰问题。

Allison Johnson
is a reviewer with 10 years of experience writing about consumer tech. She has a special interest in mobile photography and telecom. Previously, she worked at DPReview.
It’s early June and the vibes are decidedly off in Cupertino.
The hype leading up to Apple’s last two developer conferences felt much different. There was anticipation in 2023 for a potentially groundbreaking new headset. In 2024, there was a sense of urgency leading up to the company’s AI announcements and whispers that Siri might actually, finally be good at something. But 2025?
Well, things are different.
The Vision Pro was the big announcement at that 2023 show, and it’s, uh, still around. Apple has reportedly
cut production due to slow sales
, and you can
get one at a steep discount
on eBay. Maybe
the price is wrong
. And the big AI announcement last year? How’s that going? As it stands, Apple Intelligence is stalled out. The features that Apple managed to deploy
are underwhelming
, and the meaty update to Siri has been delayed —
maybe even for years
. It sounds like the whole thing was
a real fiasco
inside Apple, and publicly, the company
took down an ad
showcasing Siri features that simply don’t exist yet. Ouch.
Related
Apple Intelligence so far: did Apple oversell it?
The Vergecast’s WWDC 2025 preview
And then there’s the legal stuff. In 2021,
a court in California ordered Apple
to let developers add links allowing customers to make purchases outside of their apps. The company was also supposed to come up with a rationale for whatever commission it decided to take on those purchases.
Apple’s subsequent compliance with this order was so poor that Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers got fed up and
blocked the company from taking
any
fees
on those purchases and recommended the case for criminal contempt proceedings — all detailed in
a seething 80-page decision
. Meanwhile, in the EU, regulators
have fined Apple
for practices that fail to comply with the DMA’s antitrust rules,
Fortnite
is
back in the App Store
, and oh yeah, President Donald Trump keeps
waving tariffs around in Tim Cook’s face
with a cockamamie plan to convince him to build iPhones in the US.
What’s a beleaguered tech CEO to do in times like these? Here’s what I’d
like
to see at WWDC: Apple showing a little humility. I do not want to see a two-minute Hollywood production of Craig Federighi jumping out of a helicopter or whatever with his expensive haircut flapping in the wind. I would like to see Tim Cook take the stage and own up to the company’s recent missteps. Doesn’t he owe this particular audience some kind of apology after a judge put him on blast for choosing
the worst option for developers
at every turn? Shouldn’t he at least acknowledge that the company got out over its skis showing us Apple Intelligence demos on the same stage last year that, by some accounts,
were pure vaporware
?
I do not want to see a two-minute Hollywood production of Craig Federighi jumping out of a helicopter or whatever
It would be the right thing to do, but one early indication makes it seem unlikely Apple will choose this path.
Daring Fireball
’s John Gruber’s annual
Talk Show
episode usually features guest appearances by Apple executives who provide color on the big WWDC announcements. But Gruber says that this year, for the first time since 2015, Apple has
declined the invitation to join
. Notably, Gruber
published a blog earlier this year
taking critical aim at Apple’s mishandling of AI features. Coincidence, I’m sure!
This is a strong indicator that Apple will choose the more familiar option: project confidence and keep smiling. Instead of a sincere acknowledgement of its misjudgments, we’ll probably see it paper over the disastrous Apple Intelligence rollout with a
sleek new redesign
and
a new OS naming convention
for funsies. They’ll keep pretending that the Vision Pro is a beloved innovation and not just collecting dust on the shelves of early adopters. They’ll keep insisting that notification summaries and a text prompt image generator constitute a worthwhile AI feature set.
The new Siri capabilities featured in this demo from last year’s WWDC still haven’t arrived.
Photo: Allison Johnson / The Verge
The trouble is, I don’t think it’ll be enough this time. Apple’s force of personality has sustained it through
past missteps
, but I don’t think the same playbook will work through the current crisis. The stock price is down from its highs earlier in the year — about flat from last June — a federal judge is breathing fire at Tim Cook, and it’s obvious to anyone with an iPhone 16 that Apple Intelligence is half-baked at best. And the vibes? Way, way off.

data.title: Series C and scale
data.author: fidotron
data.article_summary: Anysphere团队宣布通过Thrive、Accel、Andressen Horowitz和DST等投资方筹集了9亿美元，用于推动AI编码研究的前沿发展。Cursor平台的年度经常性收入（ARR）已超过5亿美元，并被超过一半的福布斯500强企业使用，包括NVIDIA、Uber和Adobe。此次融资将帮助Anysphere进一步拓展AI编码研究。Anysphere实验室致力于创建更优化的编码方式，目前已具备执行这一目标的许多关键要素。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cursor公司的融资及其在AI开发工具市场中的竞争地位

不同观点：
• 一些评论对Cursor在短时间内筹集巨额资金表示惊讶，质疑资金的使用效率以及是否值得如此高估值。例如，[aduffy]提到资金可能用于用户获取和开发自有的基础模型，但对其能否比肩"三大"AI公司表示怀疑。[adwn]同样质疑Cursor是否需要如此庞大的资金，并关注其产品是否足以支撑其市场地位。
• [bix6]指出Cursor的收入倍数相对较低，并分享了对客户支持的负面体验，同时提供了其他融资信息以作对比。
• [a13n]预测开发者可能在6-12个月内回归VS Code，并认为微软作为直接竞争对手是一个巨大威胁，尤其是在其高度重视的开发者与AI领域。
• 一些评论如[bahmboo]和[xiphias2]分享了个人使用其他工具（如Roo Code和Codex web界面）的体验，并质疑Cursor是否显著优于这些工具。
• [habosa]认为Cursor可能需要开发自有模型以确保长期生存，尤其是在面对OpenAI、Anthropic和Google等强大竞争对手时。

补充讨论：
• 资金快速增长和市场竞争：[justmarc]和[mythz]提到AI领域公司之间的激烈竞争，并认为需要更多竞争者以维持价格合理。[drx]和[gsibble]则对Cursor短时间内多次融资表示关注。
• 市场动态和公司策略：[andrethegiant]和[naiv]对融资公告的发布方式和资金使用策略提出简短评论。[stonecharioteer]对公司在短时间内完成多轮融资的合理性表示不解。

争议的焦点：
• Cursor是否需要开发自有模型以保证长期竞争力。
• 短时间内筹集巨额资金的必要性和使用效率。
• 在竞争激烈的市场中，Cursor能否通过差异化产品保持市场份额。

总结来看，讨论围绕Cursor的融资策略、产品竞争力及其在AI开发工具市场中的生存与发展策略展开，参与者对Cursor的未来走向持不同看法。

data.title: Weaponizing Dependabot: Pwn Request at its finest
data.author: chha
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了如何通过“Confused Deputy”攻击利用GitHub的Dependabot（及其他机器人）进行恶意代码合并。Dependabot通常用于自动更新依赖项，但攻击者可以通过精心设计的分支名称和操作，诱使Dependabot在不知情的情况下执行恶意操作，甚至绕过分支保护规则。具体攻击步骤包括：攻击者首先 fork 目标仓库，然后在 fork 中添加恶意代码并启用Dependabot。Dependabot会基于fork中的默认分支创建更新分支，包含恶意代码。随后，攻击者向原仓库发起拉取请求（PR），并利用自动合并工作流尝试合并恶意代码。虽然首次尝试会失败，但攻击者可以进一步操作原始PR，最终实现代码注入。文章还披露了两种新的TTPs（战术、技术和程序）以增强此类攻击。

44199597.article_content:
Blog Articles
Weaponizing Dependabot: Pwn Request at its finest
Sébastien Graveline
TL;DR
: Your trusty Dependabot (and other GitHub bots) might be an unwitting accomplice. Through "Confused Deputy" attacks, they can be tricked into merging malicious code. This doesn’t stop here. It can escalate to full command injection via crafted branch names and even bypass branch protection rules. Plus, we disclose two new TTPs to build upon previously known techniques.
Introduction
Ah,
Dependabot
!
GitHub's built-in butler, tirelessly checks if your dependencies are fresh and, if not, prepares a PR with the updates. What a lifesaver, right? But, as with any cog in an automated system, there’s always the potential for rust. In this story, it is the
deputy confusion
attack.
Meet Dependabot: Your Automated Dependency Butler
So, how does this magic work? You can boss Dependabot around using a
.github/dependabot.yml
file (check out the
Dependabot options reference
).
Once active, Dependabot periodically scans your repo, guided by its config file. It also perks up and re-scans whenever you tweak this file or poke it via the
https://github.com/<Owner>/<Repo>/network/updates
tab.
When Dependabot spots an outdated dependency, it kicks off a workflow (you'll see "Dependabot Updates" pop up in your Actions tab). Then, it creates a new branch, usually named something like
dependabot/<module_type>/<registry>/<package_name>/<new_version>
. Finally, it opens a Pull Request to your default branch with all the suggested changes.
The "Confused Deputy" Problem: Wait, Who Asked You To Do That?
Now, let's talk about the
Confused Deputy Problem
. It's a classic vulnerability class (
CWE-441
, if you're into that sort of thing) where a trusted party (our "deputy") is tricked by an attacker into performing an action. The deputy thinks it’s doing honest work, but it's carrying out the attacker's nefarious plan.
Some workflows are sensitive – they might have special permissions or access to secrets, so many developers added a user check at the beginning of them. Just to make sure it was triggered by a trusted user.
Naturally, folks got a bit tired of manually approving every single Dependabot PR. "It's just a version update," they'd say. Others might say: "and we usually just end up blindly merging it anyway!". So, they created workflows to auto-merge PRs if the creator was Dependabot.
Something like this GitHub Actions workflow:
on: pull_request_target
jobs:
auto-merge:
runs-on: ubuntu-latest
if: ${
{
github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'
}}
steps:
- run:
gh pr merge
$ -d -m
Seems safe, doesn't it? After all, Dependabot is trusted, and an attacker can't just force it to open a PR on a repo they don't control… Here's the trick:
github.actor
does not always refer to the actual creator of the Pull Request. It's the user who caused the latest event that triggered the workflow.
So, if an attacker could somehow force Dependabot into making a change that triggers this auto-merge workflow, they can merge their own malicious code.
Now, an attacker can't directly command Dependabot on a repo they don't have rights to. So, what can they make Dependabot do? Let's look at the events Dependabot is able to trigger:
Event
Action
From fork
Command
pull_request_target
,
pull_request
When creating or updating a pull request.
true
@dependabot recreate
issue_comment
When showing information.
false
@dependabot show <dependency name> ignore conditions
push
When pushing to the branch, when merging etc.
false
@dependabot merge
create
When creating a new branch.
false
N/A
delete
When deleting a branch.
false
@dependabot close
workflow_run
It simply gets triggered as a side-effect of another (named) workflow running or completing.
true
Relevant if the parent workflow was triggered using one of the above commands.
The juicy one here is that Dependabot can be forced to update a Pull Request, even one originating from a fork!
Here's the evil plan:
Fork It
: Attacker forks a target repository. This repo has one of those "auto-merge if Dependabot" workflows.
Rig it
: Attacker adds their
malicious payload
to the
Default branch
of their fork.
Wake Up, Dependabot!
: Attacker enables Dependabot on their fork and adds an obviously outdated dependency to get its attention (often at the time you fork, this pre-requisite will already be met).
Dependabot Does Its Thing
: Dependabot creates its update branch on the fork. Since this branch is based on the fork's own Default branch, the now includes the attacker's payload (
through the refs/pulls/ read-only namespace
).
The Bait
: Attacker creates a Pull Request from this weaponized Dependabot branch on their fork, targeting the original (victim) repository.
Firing blanks
: This new PR triggers the auto-merge workflow in the victim repo. However, at this point,
github.actor
is the attacker, so the if condition fails, and the workflow doesn't merge anything.
Confused, are you?
: Attacker goes back to the original Pull Request in their fork
44199597.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了如何通过“Confused Deputy”攻击利用GitHub的Dependabot（及其他机器人）进行恶意代码合并。Dependabot通常用于自动更新依赖项，但攻击者可以通过精心设计的分支名称和操作，诱使Dependabot在不知情的情况下执行恶意操作，甚至绕过分支保护规则。具体攻击步骤包括：攻击者首先 fork 目标仓库，然后在 fork 中添加恶意代码并启用Dependabot。Dependabot会基于fork中的默认分支创建更新分支，包含恶意代码。随后，攻击者向原仓库发起拉取请求（PR），并利用自动合并工作流尝试合并恶意代码。虽然首次尝试会失败，但攻击者可以进一步操作原始PR，最终实现代码注入。文章还披露了两种新的TTPs（战术、技术和程序）以增强此类攻击。

data.title: A Knockout Blow for LLMs?
data.author: tu7001
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLMs）在解决中等复杂度谜题时的表现，以及其推理能力的局限性和应用前景。

不同观点：
• 一种观点认为，该论文的发现表明推理模型在中等复杂度谜题上优于非推理模型，但超过某个复杂度阈值后性能下降。作者推测这是因为模型依赖于训练数据中的模式匹配，但并未通过系统性检验训练数据或使用机械可解释性技术来验证这一假设。这种推测被一些人视为过度解读。
• 另一种观点认为，LLMs在实际应用中仍然非常有用，尽管存在极化问题和局限性。持这种观点的人强调，LLMs在激发人们热情和实际解决问题上有显著效果，不应因为其局限性而被全盘否定。
• 有人提出应发展关于LLMs能解决和不能解决哪些问题的理论，以避免不切实际的期望。这种观点认为，LLMs的复杂度视野是有限的，但通过更大规模的训练和多模态学习可以进一步拓展。
• 还有人认为不应将LLMs视为能解决所有问题的万能工具，而应根据具体问题选择合适的工具。这种观点强调AI在实际应用中的成效，而非仅仅关注其理论局限。
• 一些评论指出，LLMs的局限性如幻觉问题和推理能力有限早已为人所知，因此对这类研究的批评过于夸大。

补充讨论：
• 有评论提到LLMs可能只是实现通用人工智能（AGI）的一个组件，未来可能会有其他辅助处理器如逻辑引擎或代码解释器。
• 有人通过个人经验说明LLMs在编程等领域能显著提高生产力，即使在非其专长的领域也有应用价值。
• 讨论中还涉及对AI研究商业化前景的关注，质疑投入的资金能否带来相应的回报。
• 一些评论链接了相关的讨论和早期研究，指出快速发展的推理模型可能使某些批评过时。

争议焦点：
• 核心争议在于LLMs的推理能力是否如该论文所述主要依赖于模式匹配，以及这种局限性是否应被视为其应用价值的重大缺陷。反对者认为这种局限性被过度放大，而支持者强调应关注LLMs在实际应用中的成效。

data.author: sagyam
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：率限流算法及其在不同场景下的应用与挑战

不同观点：
• [hxtk] 提出了一种基于服务请求成本或动态学习系统容量的限流算法，认为这类算法在当前的HTTP场景下较难应用，因为需要定义成功/失败的度量标准（如延迟目标），且客户端需容忍一定概率的请求被拒绝。他还提到在Google的Zanzibar授权系统中简要提及了基于CPU时间分配的限流，但未深入讨论。

• [conradludgate] 支持使用通用信元速率算法（GCRA），认为其简单且无需后台任务和最小状态。GCRA可以作为节流实现，而不仅仅是限流器，并且可以优雅地从令牌桶转变为漏桶，通过计算空闲时间来决定何时恢复容量。

补充讨论：
• [jsw] 提到使用AIMD算法（加性增加，乘性减少）结合令牌桶，可以实现分布式进程对后端容量的自适应调整，且无需集中状态。他还认为在很多情况下，AIMD优于断路器。

• [fside] 对在实际扩展中遇到限流算法的问题感到好奇，询问是否有人因为这些问题而切换算法，并表示自己只有固定窗口限流的经验。

• [mtlynch] 对文章的呈现方式提出批评，认为文章像是未经仔细审查的AI生成内容，且在暗模式下示例显示不佳，内容被截断。

其他讨论：
• [behnamoh] 对博客中强制用户通过Google登录才能继续阅读的做法表示不解。
• [chrisweekly] 提到《HPBN》（高性能浏览器网络）一书包含相关概念，并提供了链接。
• [tonyhart7] 和 [phelm] 都提到了一篇关于限流算法的优秀文章，并提供了链接。
• [tra3] 提到尝试解释断路器和自适应并发性以提高分布式单体性能但失败，认为这些概念难以理解，并计划使用可视化工具帮助解释。
• [joshstrange] 询问在水平扩展API服务时，人们偏好使用哪些数据存储来跟踪用户/组织的请求，提到了Redis/valkey、Postgres、DynamoDB等技术。
• [onionbagle] 对是否有人实现过这些算法及其使用的技术表示好奇。
• [buggeryorkshire] 提到CGNAT曾在其以前的工作中引发许多问题，但未被提及。
• [mcdow] 对文章中的互动部分的构建技术表示好奇。

争议焦点：
• 文章的质量和呈现方式受到[mtlynch]的批评，特别是其AI生成内容的嫌疑和在暗模式下的显示问题。
• 不同限流算法的优缺点及其在实际应用中的可行性，如[hxtk]和[conradludgate]对GCRA和基于系统容量算法的讨论。

• [mtlynch] 对文章的呈现方式提出批评，认为文章像是未经仔细审查的AI生成内容，且在暗模式下示例显示不佳，内容被截断。

其他讨论：
• [behnamoh] 对博客中强制用户通过Google登录才能继续阅读的做法表示不解。
• [chrisweekly] 提到《HPBN》（高性能浏览器网络）一书包含相关概念，并提供了链接。
• [tonyhart7] 和 [phelm] 都提到了一篇关于限流算法的优秀文章，并提供了链接。
• [tra3] 提到尝试解释断路器和自适应并发性以提高分布式单体性能但失败，认为这些概念难以理解，并计划使用可视化工具帮助解释。
• [joshstrange] 询问在水平扩展API服务时，人们偏好使用哪些数据存储来跟踪用户/组织的请求，提到了Redis/valkey、Postgres、DynamoDB等技术。
• [onionbagle] 对是否有人实现过这些算法及其使用的技术表示好奇。
• [buggeryorkshire] 提到CGNAT曾在其以前的工作中引发许多问题，但未被提及。
• [mcdow] 对文章中的互动部分的构建技术表示好奇。

争议焦点：
• 文章的质量和呈现方式受到[mtlynch]的批评，特别是其AI生成内容的嫌疑和在暗模式下的显示问题。
• 不同限流算法的优缺点及其在实际应用中的可行性，如[hxtk]和[conradludgate]对GCRA和基于系统容量算法的讨论。

data.author: BUFU

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI的数据保留政策及其在法律诉讼中的影响

不同观点：
• **molf** 认为OpenAI虽然在文档中提到可以申请零数据保留（ZDR），但在实际操作中，申请往往被忽略。他怀疑这仅是市场宣传，因为多次申请未获得任何回复。
• **_jab** 指出OpenAI已经采取有效措施保护用户隐私，特别是在法律要求下。他认为如果数据泄露，应该责怪OpenAI而不是纽约时报（NYT）。
• **supriyo-biswas** 建议使用模糊哈希（如ssdeep哈希）来存储数据，而不是存储实际对话内容，以此作为一种折中方案来满足法院命令的要求。
• **sega_sai** 认为对NYT的攻击是不合理的，如果NYT有合法理由并获得法院批准，那么这种批评是没有根据的。
• **hombre_fatal** 强调LLM聊天记录泄露的潜在危害，比浏览器历史泄露更为严重，因为它展示了一个人独处时的真实想法。
• **conartist6** 批评OpenAI在解释法院命令时遗漏了一些信息，认为他们把自己描绘成无辜的一方。
• **energy123** 质疑OpenAI提供的隐私控制选项，特别是关于“设置”中的选项是否真正有效。
• **amluto** 指出“零数据保留”API的申请非常困难，普通用户很难获得。
• **atleastoptimal** 认为将数据发送到公司托管的API后会被永久记录是常识，对其他情况抱有期望是天真的。
• **yoaviram** 指责OpenAI在隐私保护上的不诚实，声称他们收费提供隐私保护，并且拒绝删除个人数据。
• **paxys** 认为法院命令实质上违反了GDPR和其他隐私法，尽管OpenAI声称在努力遵守法律。
• **nraynaud** 提到Altman收集数百万的眼部扫描数据，质疑他是否真的关心隐私。
• **WorldPeas** 关注此事件对AI编辑器隐私模式的影响，特别是企业合规使用的问题。
• **dangus** 认为法院命令保留数据是合理的，因为这涉及到版权侵权诉讼的证据，OpenAI如果不保留数据反而是销毁证据。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于OpenAI的数据保留政策是否合理以及在法律诉讼中应如何处理用户数据。
• 用户对隐私控制的期望与OpenAI实际提供的选项之间的差距也是讨论的重点。
• 有人质疑OpenAI在隐私问题上的透明度和诚信，特别是在涉及收费服务和法律要求时。
• 还有人担心LLM聊天记录泄露的潜在风险，这比传统的隐私泄露问题更为严重。
